proposals.title: Points on the table: every lost point sorted into knowledge gap or test-taking loss, each with its fix
proposals.what: SERVER: estimate.ledger(sid) for any scored sitting, and estimate.ledger_recent(learner) over the last 3 scored sittings (45 days). Every missed or blank question goes into exactly one bucket, and the first rule that matches wins. (1) Time: blank, or answered in the module's last 60 s with under 20 s on the question. (2) Grid-in entry: new scoring.entry_error(given, key) returns a rule when the typed value is the key's value in a form the grid refuses (0.66 for 2/3, '3 1/2', too short to fill the grid). (3) Second-guess: qstate.first was right and the final answer is wrong. (4) Slip: the picked option's reason is the filler 'near-miss arithmetic slip' (R9 kind slip). (5) Rushed: wrong with under 30 s on the question. (6) Execution: before this sitting the student's first-try accuracy on this template (or on topic x tier when n<3) was at least 75% over at least 3 tries ('you usually get these'). (7) Knowledge gap: everything else, carrying its misconception text. POINTS: for each bucket, rerun scoring.section_score with that bucket flipped to right and diff the band midpoints, rounded to 10. A module-1 flip that would have routed up is priced as the 580 cap lifted and shown as 'up to +N'. One 'All of it' line flips everything (560-700 -> 650-760). CONFIRM STEP, after hand-in and before the report, skippable: 'Check your 5 misses'. It serves one twin (same template and tier, new seed) per knowledge or execution miss, inline with instant feedback (source twin, cfg.inline, R24). Right in under 2x pace moves the miss to Execution (a one-off). Wrong with the same misconception makes it Confirmed (trap owed 3). Wrong with a different reason makes it Unsettled. TESTS PAGE, T1 right column: a new block 'Points on the table · last 3 sections', up to 6 rows biggest first. Each row has the bucket, the count ('4 questions'), the points ('+30') and one action: Knowledge -> 'Fix 5' (POST /api/drill {from_session, only}); Execution, Rushed or Second-guess -> 'Tight-clock module' or 'Prove'; Time -> 'Pacing module'; Grid-in entry -> 'Grid-in rules · 8 q'; Route -> 'Gate run'. Helper: 'What each kind of miss cost, recomputed with the real scoring.' Up next (T2) reads it: when the biggest bucket isn't knowledge, rule 5 changes from 'Full section' to e.g. 'Your points leak to time (50 of 120): sit a Tight-clock module'. The report shows the per-sitting ledger, and each row filters the review. WHAT THE STUDENT DOES DIFFERENTLY: after a test they spend the next session on the bucket worth the most points, instead of sitting another test or redrilling topics they already know. WHY THE SCORE MOVES: a knowledge gap and an execution loss need opposite fixes (content study versus pace and checking habits). Treating one as the other wastes the study time; pricing each in points puts the time where it pays.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's Estimated Score card ('Math 200-280 · LOW CONFIDENCE') and the report's Correct/Incorrect/Unanswered tiles and domain %. Those describe and never prescribe. Their per-question payload has no skill, difficulty or time, so they cannot tell a gap from a slip, a rushed answer or a blank, or say what any of them cost.
proposals.needs: R16 estimate.py (F4); qstate ms/first/changes (R7); attempts history per template (exists); R9 trap kinds slip/gridin plus owed; new scoring.entry_error (small); F5 drill body 'only'; S6 renders the per-sitting ledger; S3/T2 Up next reads it. The Prove, Tight-clock and Gate run actions come from proposals 2, 4 and 5 and fall back to Fix or a custom test until built.

proposals.title: Test -> Fix -> Prove: a worked-to-faded repair, then a spaced timed retest of every missed question type, with a verdict
proposals.what: After any scored sitting, a Cycle card sits at the top of /tests/ above In progress: 'Section #12 · Fix 7 -> Prove (due Sat) -> Twin', a 3-segment stepper. FIX (practice session, drill body {from_session, sequence:'faded'}). Each knowledge or confirmed miss gets three steps. (1) Worked example: the missed question itself, read-only, with the key, the rationale and the misconception behind the option the student picked, then 'Got it'. (2) Prompted twin: new seed, with a one-line cue above the stem, 'Watch for: added the exponents of y but left z alone'. (3) Unprompted twin: new seed, no cue. Execution misses skip to one timed twin (95 s answer clock). PROVE (test window, exam mode, no answers until hand-in) is due 3 days after Fix is finished, which is R9's first check-in served under the clock. It holds one slot per missed template at the original tier and format on a fresh seed, plus one control for every 2 missed slots (a template answered right in that sitting, so 'every question is one I missed' can't be inferred). It runs in ladder order at 95 s a question, with at least 6 questions; kind custom, custom.source 'proof'. VERDICT on hand-in and in the report, per misconception: 'Held under the clock ✓' / 'Held, but slow (2:40)' / 'Relapsed ✕'. Held closes the trap with closed_how 'proved' and books the 10- and 30-day check-ins; Relapsed reopens it and sends it back to Fix with the worked example. TWIN: 'Twin of Section #12' (spec kind 7) is offered in Up next at least 7 days after the original. Its report opens with a slot-by-slot comparison, 'Fixed 6 · Broke 1 · Held 15 · Still missed 3' (each a filter), and 'Change +40'. POINTS RECOVERED: the Tests header reads 'Recovered this month: +60 · 7 misconceptions proved', the ledger's what-if points of proved misconceptions deduped per template, so every gain is tied to the work that earned it. The plan (S7) puts Prove on its due day as a task: 'Prove Section #12 · 9 q · 15 min'. WHAT THE STUDENT DOES DIFFERENTLY: they don't sit test after test. Every test is followed by a repair and a timed, spaced retest before the next full section. WHY THE SCORE MOVES: worked example -> prompted -> independent is the fastest way to fix a procedure error. The delayed, timed, interleaved retest is retrieval practice with spacing, and it checks that the fix holds under the clock (fixes made in untimed practice often don't). The twin then measures the gain on the same question types.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's loop is test -> report -> nothing. Their retakes (10 to 20 a month, paid) show the same questions again, so a retake measures memory, not learning. They have no repair drill, no scheduled retest and no verdict. A finite bank can't make three fresh versions of each missed question and then a parallel form.
proposals.needs: F5 drill body: sequence 'faded', custom.source 'proof'; R9 trap due/checks/closed_how 'proved'; R24 inline; S6 twin slot comparison and verdict panel; S7 plan task; proposal 1's confirm step (optional; without it every miss goes in). Coherence fix: Tests' {kind:'twin', twin_of} and the Report's 'Retake as a test' {like: sid, full} are the same build, so keep one (twin_of).

proposals.title: Two-pass triage: Skip for now, a ranked second pass, and proof of whether it paid
proposals.what: TEST WINDOW: the question header gets 'Skip for now' (key S, the practice session's skip key, R22). It sets qstate.later=true, a state separate from Mark for review (R5), and moves on. Answering the question later clears it. The strip and navigator show Later with its own glyph (a hollow graphite chevron; new §2.3 token), the legend reads 'Later 3', and the navigator filters gain 'Later'. CHECK YOUR WORK: a first tile 'Later 3'. Above the grid, when any Later, unanswered or marked questions remain, a 'Second pass' card lists them in the order to do them: Later and unanswered by position ascending (the module runs easy -> hard, so earlier means cheaper points), then marked. Each row reads 'Q9 · 0:40 spent', and the pill 'Start second pass' walks only those questions, returning to Check your work after the last. The pacing line becomes '6:12 left · 4 in your second pass · about 1:33 each'. TIME-SINK NUDGE, Training conditions only: after 3:10 (2x pace) on one unanswered question, a quiet line under it for 6 s, '3:10 on this one. Skip for now?' [Skip for now]. It never appears under Test-day conditions. DATA: qstate._session.end_at is the elapsed ms when the student first reaches the last question or opens #review. An answer made after that is pass 2. REPORT (S6), a 'Two passes' panel: 'Pass 1: 19 answered in 27:40 · Pass 2: 3 answered, 2 right (+20) · Skipped, then right: Q14, Q19'. The sittings row gets a '2-pass +20' chip. After 3 sittings, T1 shows 'Your second passes earn 1.4 right a sitting'. WHAT THE STUDENT DOES DIFFERENTLY: they leave a stuck question after about 2 minutes, finish the ones they can answer, and come back with the time that's left. WHY THE SCORE MOVES: one stuck question can eat the time that three easier ones needed. Triage turns end-of-module blanks into answered questions, and the pass-2 numbers show the student whether the strategy works for them.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's Mark for Review, navigator and Check Your Work only let you go back. Nothing orders the second pass, flags a time sink or measures what the second pass earned, and their per-question data has no time, so they couldn't.
proposals.needs: qstate.later and _session.end_at (R7 column, S5 /state); §2.3 Later token (F1); UI.navigator state (F3); S6 report panel; the Test-day / Training conditions switch (see parity gap 'Timer mode').

proposals.title: Pace plan: checkpoints, ahead/behind on the clock, a tight-clock mode, and a personal plan built from your own times
proposals.what: LOBBY setting 'Pace plan' (with Change): Even (1:35 a question); Front-loaded (Q1-11 at 1:15 and Q12-22 at 1:55, 34:50 in all, matching the easy -> hard ladder); Mine, offered after 3 timed sittings and built from the student's median time per third of the module, scaled to 35:00. Under Test-day conditions it is off unless Pace guide is turned on. STRIP: checkpoint ticks at Q8, Q15 and Q22, with the target on hover or tap ('By Q8: 22:20 left' on Even), next to the existing pace tick. CLOCK: a DM Mono delta under the digits, '+1:20' or '-0:45', in graphite, turning --ink-deep 600 when more than 2:00 behind. It hides with the clock. Passing a checkpoint more than 2:00 behind shows one toast: '2:10 behind at Q8. Skip anything past 2:00.' BETWEEN MODULES: a 'Module 1 pace' mini chart (cumulative time against the plan line, 44px tall, 22 points). When reveal_route is on and the student routed up, it adds 'Module 2 runs harder: plan 1:45 a question after Q11'. TIMING: a new option 'Tight clock (-15%)', 29:45 a module. Like extended time, it keeps a flagged estimate but stays out of percentiles and Combined. It also gets a catalog card, 'Pacing module · 22 q · 29:45'. T1 fact row: 'Pace · finished 3 of your last 4 modules · 1:28 a question'. WHAT THE STUDENT DOES DIFFERENTLY: they know at Q8 and Q15 whether they are on track and correct early, and they train at 85% of the real time. WHY THE SCORE MOVES: blanks at the end of a module are the most avoidable lost points. Checkpoints turn one running clock into three decisions, and training faster than test pace leaves spare time on test day.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's timer is a countdown with a hide toggle: no pace information, no plan, no pace trace after a module, and only Timed or Untimed.
proposals.needs: qstate ms (R7); R34 95 s pace; a new prefs key pace_plan (R11, F4); the S5 durations function gains a 0.85 factor; reuse S6's pace chart for the between-modules mini chart; the Conditions switch.

proposals.title: The route gate: your margin to the harder module 2, gate runs, and the 580 wall made visible
proposals.what: Every scored section, paper, twin or shared sitting stores result.gate = {right, needed: ceil(0.60 x asked), margin: right - needed, cheap_misses: easy or medium misses in module 1}. BETWEEN MODULES (when 'Tell me my module 2' is on) and always in the report: 'Module 1: 13 of 22. The harder module 2 needed 14. Missed by 1, and 2 of your misses were easy or medium.' T1 replaces the plain 'Routed up 4 of 6' with 'Gate · routed up 4 of 6', plus a 6-point DM Mono dot strip of margins around a zero line, orange above it. When at least 2 of the last 3 sections routed lower, T1 adds: 'Your last sections routed lower, so they top out at 580. One more right in module 1 lifts the cap.' with 'Protect the gate · 12 q', a drill of the easy and medium templates missed in module-1 positions 1-15 of those sections, timed at 95 s. A new catalog card, 'Gate run', is module 1 alone. Its hand-in screen leads with 'Routes up · margin +2' or 'Would route lower · missed by 1', and its sittings row carries a margin chip. The How scoring works sheet gets a diagram: M1 -> 60% cut -> harder module (up to 800) or easier module (up to 580). WHAT THE STUDENT DOES DIFFERENTLY: a student around 450-600 puts their accuracy work into module-1-style easy and medium questions, not the hard ones. WHY THE SCORE MOVES: the route is the one sudden jump in the score. The lower route caps Math at 580, the College Board's own number, and the gate is won or lost on module 1's first 15 positions.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep shows 'Adaptive / Non-adaptive' as a filter label. It never says which module 2 you got, by how much you missed the other, or what that capped.
proposals.needs: scoring.route_after and ROUTE_UP_AT (exist); result.would_route (spec); R16 routed_up; F5 drill 'only' over a template list; S6 report line.

proposals.title: Calibration: spot your own misses at hand-in, and silent errors are fixed first
proposals.what: HAND-IN STEP, after 'Hand in' and before 'Marking your test…', skippable: 'Which ones do you think you got wrong?' It shows the module grid(s) at 44px; tapping a cell marks it 'Think I missed' with a graphite dashed ring, then Done or Skip. It takes about 20 s and adds nothing during the test, so Test-day conditions stay exactly like Bluebook. Stored as result.predicted_miss. CLASSIFICATION, in the report and on Tests: a miss is Spotted (predicted, or tagged Unsure/Guess when confidence tags are on) or Silent (predicted right, or tagged Sure). A right answer predicted as a miss is Underconfident. Silent errors open traps of a new R9 kind 'silent', owed 3 clean answers instead of 2, and go first in Fix and Prove. T1 fact row: 'Calibration · you spotted 4 of 7 misses · 40% -> 57% over 3 sittings'. Optional in the lobby, off by default: 'Predict your score', 200-800 in steps of 10. The report then shows 'You predicted 600 · scored 560-700'. WHAT THE STUDENT DOES DIFFERENTLY: they judge each answer, and they study the errors they didn't know they were making before the ones they already suspected. WHY THE SCORE MOVES: a suspected error gets checked, but a silent one repeats on test day. High-confidence errors that get corrected also tend to stay corrected (the hypercorrection effect), so fixing them first gives the best return.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep collects no confidence data. Mark for Review isn't analysed, and their report counts only correct, incorrect and unanswered.
proposals.needs: R9 trap kinds plus 'silent' (F4); qstate conf (R7); S6 report filter and panel; proposal 2 ordering; R16 estimate facts.

proposals.title: Calculator strategy: see where Desmos would have saved you time, and train it
proposals.what: RUNNER: per question, qstate[qid].calc_ms (time the calculator was open while that question was on screen) and calc_used (a Desmos 'change' event while it was on screen), through UI.calc observeEvent. BANK: graphable(template) for the families graphing solves (systems of linear equations, quadratic roots and vertex, intersections, exponential values, linear and quadratic inequalities, circle equations), and desmos_expressions(item), which turns the item's params into Desmos expressions. Start with the families whose params already hold explicit equations. REPORT, review only and never during a test: on a graphable question, 'Solve in Desmos' opens the docked calculator loaded with the expressions (setState) and a one-line method, e.g. 'Graph both lines; the x of the intersection is the answer'. A panel reads: 'Graphable questions 11 · calculator used on 4 · by hand 2:10 avg · with the calculator 0:55 avg'. CATALOG: a 'Calculator-first module' card, 11 graphable questions at 60 s each, in practice mode, showing the Desmos route after each answer. The spec's No-calculator tool stays for the opposite kind of training. WHAT THE STUDENT DOES DIFFERENTLY: they learn which question shapes to give to Desmos and stop solving systems and quadratics by hand. WHY THE SCORE MOVES: the calculator is allowed on every digital SAT Math question. Seconds saved on graphable questions become time for the hard questions at the end of module 2.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep embeds the same Desmos panel with no guidance and no usage data, and forgets its state.
proposals.needs: Bank work (T-bank): the graphable flag and an expression builder per family; UI.calc observeEvent and setState (F3); qstate fields (R7); S6 report panel; the Desmos production key (open question 15).

proposals.title: Elimination intelligence: the traps you reject, and the ones that survive
proposals.what: At finish, for each multiple-choice question, qstate[qid].struck and the answer trail (R7) are read against Item.reasons. Rejected = the reasons behind the struck distractors. Survivor = the picked option's reason, when at least one option was struck and the pick was wrong. key_struck = the key was struck at any point. REPORT player (S6): 'You crossed out A and C, then chose D: added the exponents of y but left z alone.' and, when it applies, 'You crossed out the right answer (B), then undid it.' TESTS and REVIEW: a 'Survivor traps' list, the top 5 over 30 days, each with the misconception text, 'survived your elimination 3 times', the topic, and 'Contrast drill · 6 q'. The drill serves twins whose choices carry that misconception's option, and its feedback names both finalists: 'Your two finalists: the key, and used the diameter as the radius'. 'Traps you reliably reject' (struck at least 3 times, never picked) shows as a strength on the skill panel. When it has happened, a line reads 'Crossed out the right answer 2 times in 3 sittings · cross out only what you can show is wrong'. WHAT THE STUDENT DOES DIFFERENTLY: they practise telling apart the two options they keep getting torn between. WHY THE SCORE MOVES: medium questions are often lost at the final choice between the key and one plausible trap. Naming that trap turns 'careless' into a specific pair the student can train.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep saves eliminations to its server (seen in their bundle) and shows nothing from them. Their distractors are prose 'Distractor Analysis', not labels, so they can't be counted across sittings.
proposals.needs: qstate.struck and trail (R7); Item.reasons; R9 traps norm; the F5 drill body gets a 'reason' filter, which needs a survey of which seeds carry which normalised reason (like blueprint.survey); S6 report.

proposals.title: Paper crowd view: how the field did on each question, and your should-get misses
proposals.what: For papers (the same questions for everyone), once you have finished the paper (Discussion's gate): each question, in the report and in a new 'Questions' tab of the Discussion sheet, shows its '% right' among first standard sittings (n at least 20, otherwise 'Not enough sittings yet · 12'). It shows the spread of picks A-D, each wrong option with its misconception ('B 31% · added the exponents of y but left z alone'), and 'Median time of right answers 1:12 · yours 2:40'. SHOULD-GET MISSES are questions at least 70% of the field got right that you missed. They are listed first in the report's paper panel and as the sitting's first ledger row, with Fix. 'Where you beat the field' lists questions under 40% of the field got right that you got right. Discussion is anchored to questions: each question row shows its post count and a pinned 'Methods' post (the most Helpful one), and posting from a row fills in About. Paper cards (T5) add 'Hardest: M2 harder Q19 · 18% right'. WHAT THE STUDENT DOES DIFFERENTLY: they fix first the questions most peers get right, and compare their time with the field's median on each question. WHY THE SCORE MOVES: how many others got a question right says more about priority than your own miss list, and a per-question time benchmark shows where your method, not your knowledge, is slow.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's Comments are unmoderated, unanchored chatter with spoilers, and 'People took N' is their only crowd number.
proposals.needs: Paper-sitting attempts flagged as first standard sittings (S5 stats, R16 rule); R8 guess and repeat rows excluded; S6 report panel; this section's Discussion sheet. Coherence: Compete's Weekly Module is also a weekly test-window test, so decide whether the weekly paper and the Weekly Module are one event or two.

proposals.title: An estimate calibrated against real Bluebook and SAT scores
proposals.what: Today's 'Add a score' (S3 /api/scores) already records Bluebook practice tests and official scores. A PAIR is a logged Math score and a standard SAT Freshman section within 10 days of each other. PER STUDENT, once one pair exists, T1 shows 'Your Bluebook test: 610 (Sep 20) · our estimate then: 560-700 · we read 20 low for you' and 'Adjusted: 580-720'. GLOBAL: once there are at least 50 pairs across students, a nightly tools/calibrate.py refits scoring.ANCHORS (earned/possible -> reported score, least squares) as a new version. The How scoring works sheet then says 'Calibrated against 312 Bluebook scores (Sep 2026)'; below 50 it says 'Not yet checked against real scores'. The fit's spread replaces the fixed ±70 when it is smaller, so the band narrows as evidence grows. WHAT THE STUDENT DOES DIFFERENTLY: they set their target gap and how often they test from a number that has been checked against the real test. WHY THE SCORE MOVES: a plan built on an estimate 50 points off spends time in the wrong place. Calibration makes the estimate more accurate, and that improves every decision built on it (proposals 1, 2 and 5).
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's estimate is uncalibrated ('Math 200-280 · LOW CONFIDENCE'), drops floor sections and is never compared with official practice tests.
proposals.needs: S3 added scores; R16 estimate.py; versioned scoring.ANCHORS (F4); a new tool; pairs used only in aggregate.

proposals.title: Second look: retry your misses before you see the key (slip vs gap)
proposals.what: After the final hand-in, the test window shows a new screen, #second, instead of redirecting. It is skipped for the diagnostic, contests and sittings with 0 misses and 0 blanks. h1 "Before you see the answers". Line: "You missed 7 and left 3 blank. Try them again with no clock. It tells a slip from a gap." Two chip rows show positions only: misses as filled chips (M1 Q9, M1 Q14, M2 Q3 ...) and blanks as dashed chips. Pill "Try them again (10)" (Enter) and quiet "Skip to my report". Pressing it opens the runner in exam mode over just those questions, using the P4 queue footer ("Second look · 3 of 10"). There is no clock; Elapsed counts up. Calculator, reference, highlights, notes and eliminations come back as they were. The original pick is hidden so it can't steer the retry, with the line "Your test answer is hidden". Each answer goes to POST /api/session/{sid}/second {question_id, answer, ms}, is stored as qstate[qid].second {given, right, ms}, and is filed to attempts with repeat=1 (R8), so mastery and the score never change. "Finish second look" can end it at any point. Second look closes for good the first time the report is opened with keys (qstate._session.second_closed). The report then tags every miss: "Slip · right on second look" or "Gap · wrong again", with "same trap twice" when both picks name the same misconception. Blanks get "Out of time · right untimed" or "Couldn't do it". The report's Fix drills only Gaps by default. Slips also feed P2 and P3 ("slips cost about 30 points").
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's review modal. It shows the Correct answer box straight away, and 'Hide answers' only hides it; you can never re-answer. So their report can't tell a careless slip from a real gap, and every miss looks the same. We can re-serve the exact item by (template, seed) before any key is shown, and the misconception on the second wrong pick shows whether it is the same trap.
proposals.needs: F4: qstate.second, attempts repeat=1 (R8). S5: POST /second and 409 once closed; /finish returns missed and blank positions (result.modules). F3: runner queue plus untimed exam mode (shared with P4). S6: report slip/gap tags, Fix defaults to Gaps, and setting second_closed on the first keyed GET. Report's what-if for the points on slips.

proposals.title: Points on the table: where your next 50 points are, on the score card
proposals.what:
T1 (Estimated score) gets a third block under the facts, titled "Where your next points are". It holds up to 4 rows from estimate.levers(learner), which re-scores the last 3 scored sittings with scoring.section_score under one change at a time. Rows are ranked by points:
(a) "Easy and medium misses · 6 in 3 tests · about +40": those misses flipped to right, averaged over the sittings. Action: "Fix 6" (a drill on those templates with new seeds).
(b) "Route · 1 more right in module 1 on Sep 12 would have earned the harder module 2 and lifted the 580 cap". Shown when a lower route fell within 2 questions of the 60% cut. Action: "Sit module 1".
(c) "Recurring trap · 'squared only the first term' · 3 tests · about +20": open traps hit in 2 or more sittings. Action: "Fix it".
(d) "Slips · 4 right on second look · about +20", from P1. Action: "Turn on the pace guide", which toggles the pref inline.
Each row has a label (600 14px), evidence (DM Mono 13px soft), a points chip on --wash ("+40", rounded to 10, prefixed with the approximately sign) and a .btn action. A sum line reads "Worth about +80 · 560–700 → 640–780 · your 700 target is inside". It is drawn on UI.scale: the current band, the lever band as an outline, and the target tick. A quiet "How this is counted" opens #howScored at the what-if paragraph. Empty: "Sit a full section to see where your points are." Loading and error follow T1.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's Estimated Score card. It shows 'Math 200-280' and a red LOW CONFIDENCE chip, and never says how to raise the number. Ours turns the gap to target into ranked, costed actions that start in one tap. Their per-question data has no skill, difficulty or misconception, so they can't compute this.
proposals.needs: F4: estimate.py gains levers(), reusing Report's what-if re-score (scoring.py) plus traps. F5: drill body with a template list (§2.6). F1: UI.scale. P1 feeds the slips row (optional). S5 renders it on /tests/.

proposals.title: Test habits: how you take tests, measured from the runner
proposals.what:
A full-width card titled "How you take tests", placed under T1 and T2. It reads the last 6 finished timed sittings. With fewer than 2: "Sit 2 timed tests to see your habits: pacing, blanks, answer changes and confidence." The server's tests.habits(learner) is returned in GET /api/tests.habits. Each row is {id, verdict good|costs, title, evidence, series, points, action}. A row shows a glyph (check for good, ! for costs, ink only), a title (600 15px), an evidence line (DM Mono 13px), a 60x20 sparkline across the sittings and one action. The habits and their triggers:
- Answer changes: right to wrong vs wrong to right, from qstate first vs final. Example: "Changes cost you: 7 right→wrong, 3 wrong→right". Action: "See the changes" (report ?filter=changed).
- Finish margin: seconds left at each module hand-in. "4 of 12 modules ran to 0:00", or the good "You kept 4:10 on average to check". Action: the pace guide toggle.
- Front-loaded time: the share of the module spent on the first third (the easy tiers) vs the P5 budgets.
- Blanks: the average per module, and the points lost against guessing at 25%.
- Sure but wrong, when confidence tags are used: "5 Sure answers were wrong; 3 were 'flipped the inequality'". Action: "Fix that trap".
- Guess accuracy vs the 25% chance rate, which shows whether eliminating works.
- Away from the window: the count and the time.
- Marked but never revisited, from the visit trail.
Rows that cost points come first, sorted by points. 4 show, then "Show all 7". Each has a "Why" popover stating its rule. On a phone, rows stack with the chart under the text.
proposals.beats: None. TopTierPrep records nothing about how a student sits a test: their per-question payload has no time spent, and a reload resets the stopwatch. Our qstate (ms, first, changes, conf, away, marks) becomes coaching on how to take the test, which no fixed-paper site offers.
proposals.needs: F4: qstate fields per R7, plus result.modules[].left_s written at each hand-in (S5 finish). S5: habits() in api_tests.py, included in GET /api/tests. F1: a tiny sparkline in charts.js. S6: the report's ?filter=changed deep link. P5 budgets for front-loading, and P1 for slips (both optional).

proposals.title: Check your work: 'Go through them' queue and jump keys
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's Check Your Work page and module navigator. A cell jumps to one question, and getting back costs two more taps each time. Ours walks every blank and marked question in order in one pass, with live counts.
proposals.needs: F3: runner.js navigator and queue (client only; the same queue drives P1). F2: UI.keys entries U and Shift+M. No server change.

proposals.title: Pace guide that follows the module's ladder and your own speed
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's timer (and Bluebook's) is a bare countdown. An even pace is wrong advice on a module that runs easy to hard, and they can't personalise it: they don't keep time per answer, and a reload resets the stopwatch. Ours tells the student, question by question, whether they are banking time for the hard end.
proposals.needs: S5: payload.pace computed in api_tests.py from attempts.ms (R7 passes test ms into attempts). F3: the strip tick and the delta line. F4: prefs test_pace changes from bool to off|even|ladder in the prefs registry (R11).

proposals.title: Solve first: cover the choices until you have an answer
proposals.what: A tool and setting, "Solve first: cover the choices". It appears in the start sheet's Tools step, as a lobby row and as a More toggle; the pref test_solve_first is shared with the practice session and off by default. When it is on, multiple-choice options render as one covered --tile-2 block at their final height, reading "Choices covered · work it out, then reveal (V)". "Reveal choices" (the V key, free in the runner map) uncovers them for that question, and they stay uncovered on later visits. Grid-ins are unaffected. qstate[qid] stores covered: true and reveal_ms, the time before the reveal. Scoring is unchanged, and the sitting keeps its estimate (result.solve_first is recorded for information). The report adds a line: "Solved first on 18 of 22 · 86% right · 1 trap pick, against 4 on questions where you looked first". Per question it shows "Revealed after 1:05". On a phone the covered block is a single 120px tile; tap to reveal.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep has only the ABC eliminator, and their 'Distractor Analysis' is prose you read afterwards. Ours trains the one habit that beats trap answers. Because every wrong option names a misconception, it also measures how many trap picks the habit prevented, which their bank cannot know.
proposals.needs: F3: a covered state in UI.workspace. F4: qstate keys and the prefs key test_solve_first. F2: key V. S6: the report line and the per-question reveal time.

proposals.title: How everyone did: a per-question crowd view for Papers
proposals.what:
Once you have finished a paper, its Discussion sheet opens on a new first tab: How everyone did · Discussion 12. The header reads "From 214 first sittings". Below 20 first sittings it reads "Needs 20 first sittings · 12 so far". Sort choices: Hardest for everyone / Where you beat the crowd / Where the crowd beat you / In order.
- Each row: the "M1 Q17" chip, the skill, "18% right" with a bar, your result glyph, and median time against yours ("1:50 · you 3:10").
- Expanding a row shows UI.spread of A–D: each option's share plus its misconception ("41% · divided only one side by 2"), with your pick marked. For a grid-in it shows the top 3 wrong values.
- Row actions: "Try one like this" (an inline drill of that template with a new seed, R24), "Discuss" (Discussion filtered to that question) and "Open my review".
- A top block, "Fooled the most people", lists the 3 questions with the lowest right rates.
- Module 2 questions not on your route sit in a collapsed "Not on your route" group.
- After you have sat it, the paper card gains the line "Hardest: M2 Q19 · 18% right · you got it".
- Posts tagged to a question show that question's % right beside the chip.
Server: GET /api/papers/{n}/crowd is gated like posts. Per question it aggregates the same first sittings as sat_by: {n, right, picks[4] | top_wrong[3], median_ms}. Misconception labels are read server-side from the paper's stored items. It is cached for 10 minutes, like drill.levels.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's 'People took 1.6k' tile and Comments modal. A head count and unmoderated, spoiler-filled chatter are their only crowd signals, with nothing per question. Ours shows where you stand on every question and which named misconception caught the crowd, and one tap practises that trap.
proposals.needs: S5: the crowd endpoint and aggregation in api_tests.py. F1: UI.spread (already listed in charts.js). F5/R24: the inline twin drill source. S6 (optional): the crowd bar in the review of paper sittings. It works unchanged if papers become twin papers (see parity gaps), because it aggregates per slot and per reason.

proposals.title: The hand-in moment: an earned result before the report
proposals.what:
Final hand-in no longer shows the 'Marking your test…' skeleton and redirects. It shows #done in the test window. /finish returns {finished, estimate {low, high, previous, best}, route, moments[], misses, blanks}.
- k "Full section #12 · handed in".
- The band on UI.scale (200–800), with the previous band as a ghost outline and the target tick. The numbers count up once over 600ms; with reduced motion they are static.
- A headline: "Up 40 since Sep 12", "Level with Sep 12" or "Your first estimate".
- A route chip ("Harder module 2"), always shown now that the test is over.
- Up to 2 earned moments from a fixed list, each a line with our trophy or marks icon: first route to the harder module 2, a new best band, no blanks, beat Paper #8's average (540), every module finished with 3:00 or more left, a twin beating its original by 30 or more, first High confidence. Nothing shows when nothing is earned.
- Actions: pill "See your report" (Enter); .btn "Second look (10)" when P1 is available; quiet "Fix 7 now"; quiet "Back to Tests".
Unscored kinds read "17 of 22 right · practice, no estimate". The diagnostic keeps its sign-up gate (R38). Offline, it keeps the spec's 'Handing in when you reconnect' state.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep drops you onto /results with count-up rings and a 'Practice test — not ranked' pill. It makes no comparison with last time and marks no firsts. Ours earns its moment with facts: the change, the route and real firsts, and puts the next useful action one key away.
proposals.needs: S5: the /finish response fields. F4: estimate.py (R16). S1: the achievements engine (R25), where the test moments are registered. F1: UI.scale. P1 for the Second look button.

proposals.title: Thumb-first test window on phones (and right-click strike on desktop)
proposals.what:
At under 760px:
(1) Swiping the question column left or right (at least 64px, angle under 30°, never while text is selected, while Highlights & Notes is on, or inside a .q-table scroller) moves Next or Back with a 160ms slide, and none with reduced motion.
(2) Long-pressing an option for 450ms strikes or unstrikes it without Eliminate mode. A ring fills to show progress, and navigator.vibrate(8) fires where supported.
(3) The footer becomes [‹ Back 44px] [Mark 44px, bookmark icon, aria-pressed] [M1 · 7 of 22 ⌃] [Next pill], so Mark for review is within thumb reach, not in the top header.
(4) Swiping up on the footer button opens the navigator sheet, which carries P4's "Go through 8".
(5) Grid-ins get an optional answer pad pinned above the footer: 0–9, '.', '/', '−' and ⌫, in 4 rows of 44px keys. The OS keyboard no longer covers the stem, and the minus a decimal pad lacks is there. A "Use the answer pad" toggle is remembered in localStorage.
(6) The calculator sheet snaps as specced, with the question scrolling above it.
On desktop, right-clicking an option strikes it; the context menu is suppressed on options only.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's runner is a desktop Bluebook clone. Eliminating needs the ABC toggle and then a tap on a small circle, Mark for Review sits at the top of the screen, and grid-in entry relies on the OS keyboard. Ours strikes in one long-press, marks by thumb, and enters grid-ins without covering the question.
proposals.needs: F3: runner.js/runner.css gestures, footer layout and the answer pad; the UI.workspace strike hook. No server change.

proposals.title: Your working, kept per question: calculator log and scratch pad, replayed in review
proposals.what:
(a) Calculator log. On each question change, if Desmos changed, the runner diffs getState().expressions and stores the new or edited ones for the question just left: qstate[qid].calc = {open_ms, exprs [latex, 20 at most, 200 chars each]}. It opens a Desmos folder named "Q8" for the next question, so the list stays readable.
(b) Scratch pad (tool "Scratch", key W, free in the runner map). A transparent canvas over the column with Pen, Marker, Eraser and Clear, for touch, stylus or mouse. Strokes are simplified (Ramer–Douglas–Peucker, 1px) and stored per question as qstate[qid].ink (30 KB at most), sent through the save queue.
(c) Review. The report's player shows a "Your working" block under the question: a read-only Desmos with that question's expressions, and the ink laid over the stem, beside the misconception your pick named. The student sees where the method went wrong.
P2 also uses calc open_ms ("calculator open on 70% of questions").
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's Desmos panel forgets its state, and nothing keeps a student's working, so their review can only show the key and prose. Ours shows your own steps next to the named mistake.
proposals.needs: F3: UI.calc hooks (getState/setState are already specced) and a new canvas component. F4: qstate cap raised to about 200 KB per sitting. S5: /state accepts calc and ink. S6: the report player renders them read-only.

proposals.title: Compare any two sittings, with a slot-by-slot diff for twins and retakes
proposals.what:
In T6 (Your sittings), each row gets a "Compare" checkbox; X toggles it on the focused row. With two ticked, a bar appears: "Compare #11 and #14" [Compare] [Clear]. The compare sheet is 720px wide, full height on a phone.
- Two columns: band, M1, M2, route, time used, blanks, away and pauses.
- Domain bars side by side for the 4 domains (earned / possible).
- A "Question types" table that joins the two sittings by template, in three groups: Missed both times ("same trap" when the reason matched), Fixed (missed in the older sitting, right in the newer) and New misses. Each group has a Fix action.
- For a twin and its source, or a paper retake, the table is slot by slot (M1 Q1..Q22) with a ✓/✕ glyph per side and a summary: "Fixed 5 · Still missed 2 · New 1 · +60".
The twin's T6 row also carries a chip, "vs #11: +60 · fixed 5". Deep link: /tests/?compare=11,14.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's /results list. It shows no score on its cards, can't compare sittings, and a fixed paper can't be re-sat fresh. Our twins make the comparison fair, the same question types at the same positions, so 'did I improve?' gets a real answer.
proposals.needs: S5: GET /api/compare?a=&b= (owner-only), from stored templates, reasons and result.modules. S6: /api/history fields (R26). F1: UI.sheet. F2: key X on /tests/.

parity_gaps.spec_says: Papers #1–#7 plus one new paper each Monday. Everyone gets identical questions, as on TopTierPrep, which is what makes Sat by, Average, the percentile and Discussion comparable.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It is their paper grid plus a weekly refill. Identical questions also mean answers can be passed around, which inflates the percentile the paper exists to give. The user already rejected that for the Daily Challenge (twins, v2-decisions #1).
parity_gaps.upgrade: Twin papers. Every sitter gets the same template, tier and format in every slot, with their own seed, using blueprint.twin/draw_matching, which the spec already has. Crowd stats, rating and percentile still compare like with like per slot, and the P7 crowd view aggregates per slot and per misconception. Discussion becomes about method, not '(C) is 12', so the spoiler gate matters less. 'New to you' changes to 'question types new to you'. Exact copies stay only for friend Shares.

proposals.title: Pressure check: an untimed twin round after hand-in that separates what you don't know from points the clock took
proposals.what:
SCREEN: after the final POST /finish of any timed sitting (section, paper, twin, shared, module, custom), the Handing-in step shows #pressure before the redirect. h1 'Before your score: a pressure check'. Line: '9 questions like the ones you missed, left blank, guessed or spent over 3:10 on. Same kind, same difficulty, new numbers, no clock.' Tiles: Missed 5 · Blank 2 · Guessed 1 · Slow 1. Pill 'Start the check · about 12 min'. Quiet 'See my score now'. If skipped, the report keeps offering 'Pressure check · 9' for 7 days.
WHICH QUESTIONS: every qid that was wrong, blank, tagged conf='guess' (right or wrong), or whose qstate.ms is over 2 x 95 s x the timing factor. Cap 15, one per template, in module and position order.
BUILD: POST /api/drill {source:'pressure', parent:sid, feedback:'end', timing:'off'}. Each slot is blueprint.draw_matching(b, template, tier, fmt), a fresh seed. cfg.inline=true (R24), so it is never listed and is counted on the parent. cfg.pressure_of maps each twin qid to its original qid. It runs in the runner in exam mode: nothing revealed, a count-up clock, ms recorded per question.
CLASSIFY (server pressure.classify(parent, drill), one verdict per original question):
- Knowledge gap: the twin was also wrong, with the same misconception (same norm, R9). Shown as 'Real gap: <label>'.
- Shaky: the twin was wrong a different way, or a grid-in was wrong.
- Speed: the twin was right but took over 2x pace. 'You can do it, not yet at test speed.'
- Pressure: wrong or blank in the test, twin right at pace.
- Lucky: right in the test with conf=guess, twin wrong.
- Confirmed: guessed right, twin right.
STORED on the parent: result.pressure {buckets:{knowledge:[qid], shaky, speed, pressure, lucky, confirmed}, ceiling}. ceiling is the band from scoring.section_score with the Pressure questions counted right. When module 1 changes route, it reads 'would have routed up'.
REPORT BLOCK (S6 renders; this section supplies the data): a stacked bar with counts and glyphs, e.g. 'Knowledge 3 · Speed 1 · Pressure 3 · Lucky 1'. Line: 'Your band today 540-680. Without the 3 pressure losses: 580-720.' Each bucket lists its M1 Q7-style chips and has one fix:
- Knowledge: 'Fix these 3' (pool:'redo', those traps).
- Speed: 'Timed sprint · 6 at 95 s' (templates, timing:'pace').
- Pressure: 'Next test with the pace guide' (sets prefs.pace and opens the start sheet).
- Lucky: 'Practise 5 like it'.
TESTS PAGE: the sittings row gets the chip 'Pressure 3 · Knowledge 3' and a 'Has pressure losses' filter.
RULES: the twins' answers file as normal attempts (source pressure) and count toward mastery. They never change the sitting's band, percentile or paper stats.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's report only splits Correct / Incorrect / Unanswered, and even that contradicts itself (25 Wrong vs 0 Incorrect / 45 Unanswered). It can never say why a question was lost. Re-testing needs the same question at the same difficulty with new numbers. A fixed 29-paper bank can't make that; it could only re-show the exact item, whose answer the student has already seen.
proposals.needs: S5 blueprint.twin/draw_matching; F5 drill body: source 'pressure' with parent, cfg.inline and feedback 'end'; F4 qstate ms/conf (R7) and traps norm (R9) for the same-misconception match; scoring.section_score for the ceiling; S6 report renders result.pressure; prefs.pace (R11). Keep it subject-aware (per-section buckets) so R&W slots in later (v2 decision 3).

proposals.title: Projected score from practice and 'Where your next points are', on the Tests page
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's Estimated Score is empty until you sit a full test or module ('Complete a full-length test or a practice module to get your score estimate'). It never breaks down where points would come from, and their plan's 'Score gap' is just target minus current. Every one of our practice answers is tied to a template with known blueprint slots, so practice alone projects a section and prices each skill in points.
proposals.needs: F4 estimate.py (R16): projected() and gains(); attempts' template/difficulty/fmt (these exist) and the R8 flags; blueprint.slots/abilities/by_domain and scoring.route_after/section_score (exist); proposal 5 (route-up trainer) as a link target. S7 Plan and S3 Today can read gains() for Focus and Try one. Keyed per section so R&W is additive.

proposals.title: Trap test: a timed test where your own past misconceptions are among the wrong answers
proposals.what:
CARD: a T4 card 'Trap test' and a start-sheet step 1 option.
- Tags: Your traps · Test rules.
- Facts: '10-22 questions · 95 s each'.
- Helper: 'Every question offers a wrong answer you've fallen for before. Do you still take it?'
- Stats: 'Traps ready 14' (open, plus fixed ones due a check-in, plus fixed within 60 days) and 'Last trap test: took 3 of 12'.
STEP 2:
- 'Which traps': All ready 14 / Open 9 / Check-ins due 5 / Pick (a checklist of trap labels with topic glyph and 'hit 3x').
- Length: 10 / 22 / all.
- 'Neutral questions mixed in': 1 in 4 (default) / none.
BUILD: for each trap (template, norm), the drill body want {template: regex(norm)} walks up to 40 seeds for an item where a distractor's reason matches. When the template can't, pool 'related' takes a sibling template that carries the same norm. The neutral slots come from the same skills, with none of your traps on offer, so the test isn't transparent. Ladder order, 95 s a question, no reveal until hand-in, calculator as your defaults.
It is kind 'custom' with cfg.custom.source 'traps'. Not scored (no estimate), listed as 'Trap test' (UI.KIND).
MARKING per question: trap taken (the chosen option's reason is the trap), other wrong, right, or blank.
RESULT (S6 renders; data from S5):
- Headline: 'Your traps were on offer 14 times. You took them 3 times.' History: 'Last time: 7 of 12 (Sep 2)'.
- One row per trap: the label, 'offered 2 · taken 0' with glyphs, and the change: 'Check-in passed' / 'Still open' / 'Relapsed'.
- A right, non-guess answer with the trap on offer counts as a clean check-in (R9). Taking the trap reopens it.
UP NEXT (T2): offer a trap test when 5 or more check-ins are due, or 8 or more traps are open, and none was sat in the last 7 days.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's wrong options carry a prose 'Distractor Analysis' written after the fact. Nothing is indexed per student, so they can't choose questions by which wrong answer tempts you, and their Redo list just replays the same item. Every option in our bank names its misconception, and any template can be walked to a seed that offers a specific one.
proposals.needs: F4 traps with norm and check-ins (R9); F5 drill body `want` and pool 'related' (§2.6); S5 blueprint.custom with queue; open question 18 (a stable misconception tag per option) makes the matching exact. Until then the number-stripped norm is used. S10 Review consumes the check-ins; S6 renders the block; F1 UI.KIND 'Trap test'.

proposals.title: Personal pacing: a pace line from your own timing, time-sink nudges and a triage on Check your work
proposals.what:
SETTING: 'Pacing coach' in the start sheet's Tools and the lobby, off by default; stored as prefs.coach. When on, the sitting gets cfg.coach, a 'Coached' pill on the report, and is left out of percentiles and paper stats. It still gets an estimate.
PERSONAL PACE LINE (whenever Pace guide is on):
- GET /api/session adds pace: [s1..s22], one per position, with no template names.
- Each value is your median first-try seconds on that template (at least 3 timed answers), else on that tier in that domain, else the tier default (easy 70, medium 95, hard 125).
- The values are scaled so the module sums to its duration minus a 3:00 reserve.
- The strip's amber tick sits at the question you should be on. Under the clock, in DM Mono 12px: '2:05 ahead' or '1:40 behind'. It hides with the clock.
- The lobby shows the plan: 'Q1-8 by 26:00 left · Q9-16 by 13:30 · Q17-22 by 3:00 · 3:00 to check'.
TIME-SINK NUDGE (coach on, timed only):
- Trigger: time on the current question passes max(2 x pace[i], 2:30).
- A 40px --wash banner under the question header: '3:10 on this one. Your pace for it is 1:20. Mark it and come back?' [Mark and next] [Keep going].
- Once per question, announced in the live region, never a modal.
CHECK YOUR WORK TRIAGE (coach on):
- Above the grid: 'Spend your 6:12 like this'.
- The unanswered and marked questions, ordered by p(right) / expected seconds. p is your first-try accuracy on that kind and tier, shown only as a number.
- Rows: 'Q18 · unanswered · about 1:10 · you get 80% of these', 'Q21 · marked · about 3:00 · 35% · guess and move'. A row opens its question.
REPORT: the report gets a 'Time sinks' line (S6 renders): '3 questions took 9:40 together; 2 were wrong'.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's runner, like Bluebook, has only a countdown and a hide toggle. Their QBank stopwatch resets on reload, and their report payload has no time per question at all. They give no pace target, no warning when one question is eating the clock, and no advice on how to spend the last minutes.
proposals.needs: F4 qstate.ms and attempts.ms (R7); a pace(learner, questions, factor) helper in S5 api_tests; F3 runner strip, banner and review triage slot; F4 prefs key 'coach' (R11); F4 estimate.percentile excludes cfg.coach (R16); S6 time-sink line.

proposals.title: Route-up trainer and harder-module gauntlet: fresh module drills with a live goal
proposals.what:
TRAINER CARD (T4 'Route-up trainer'; shown while your route-up rate is under 80%, or before any section):
- Tags: Module 1 · Official timing · Never repeats. Facts '22 questions · 35 min'.
- Goal: 'Route up 3 times in a row'. Pips for the last 5 trainer sittings (filled = routed up), plus 'Best streak 2'.
EACH SITTING is kind module with cfg.module 'm1' and cfg.trainer 'route'.
- Lobby fact: 'The line: 14 of 22 right routes you up'.
- The hand-in block says '13/22 · 1 short of the harder module 2'. A 22-cell strip marks where the 14th right answer would be.
- 'These cost the route: Q2 (easy), Q5 (easy)' lists the easiest misses that make up the gap, each with 'Try a twin'.
- Pill 'Fix what cost the route' (POST /api/drill {from_session, only:[those qids], each:2}). Quiet 'Next module 1'.
ROUTE MARGIN everywhere a section or paper appears (sittings row chip, report hero line): 'Routed up with 2 to spare' or '1 short'. It is module 1's right count minus ceil(0.6 x asked).
GAUNTLET CARD (shown when the target is 620 or more, or after 2 upper routes): 'Harder module 2 gauntlet' · Fixed · Leans hard.
- Goal '18 of 22 on the harder module 2', with the last 5 results.
- A hard-question table by skill over the gauntlet sittings ('Circles, hard: 2 of 5') with 'Practise hard' per row.
STREAKS count only official timing on the standard module 1 tier.
LISTS: the history Kind filter adds 'Trainer'. Plan can schedule 'Route-up trainer' as a test task.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep gives a free student 1 exam attempt, and even paid tiers resit the same fixed module 1 of a paper. Nowhere does it show how close module 1 came to the upper route, which is what decides whether a score can pass 580. Only an unlimited generator can serve a fresh module 1 every time you want to try again.
proposals.needs: Module kinds m1/m2u and cfg.trainer on POST /api/mock/new (S5); scoring.route_after and ROUTE_UP_AT (exist); F5 drill from_session + only + each; S6 history rows with modules[] and the report margin line; S7 Plan task (optional).

proposals.title: Twin rematch with a slot-by-slot diff, and twin shares so friends compare without passing answers around
proposals.what:
TWIN DIFF (on hand-in of a twin_of sitting):
- The report handoff opens a block, 'Same test, new numbers'.
- Two aligned rows of 44 cells: Original #11 · Sep 12, and Twin · today. Each column's tooltip gives the skill and difficulty.
- Legend with counts: Fixed 6 · Held 33 · Still missing 3 · New misses 2. Each count is a filter.
- Each 'still missing' slot says whether the misconception repeated ('Same trap both times: forgot to square the radius') or changed.
- Headline: '+60 on an equal test: 520-660 → 580-720'.
CHAINS: twins can chain ('3rd sitting of this form'), with a small band chart of that form across its sittings. Every sittings row gets 'Twin again'.
TWIN SHARE: the share sheet (2.9) gains 'What they sit':
- Twin (default): 'The same kinds of question in the same order, with their own numbers. Answers can't be passed around, and you still compare question by question.'
- Exact: 'The same questions as yours.'
PEERS: after both have finished, each peer row gets a slot grid: 'Q7 · a line touching a parabola: you ✓ · Ana ✕ · she picked: forgot to halve c'. Only the misconception label is shown, never the peer's raw answer, and only after both have finished.
CLASSES: a teacher's 'Assign a test' defaults to a twin for each student.
proposals.beats: A retake on TopTierPrep is the same paper with the same questions, so it measures memory, and nothing compares two sittings question by question. Their share exists only for QBank sessions (and froze the page), and assigning a test is hidden in an unlinked teacher area. A fixed bank can't produce a parallel form on demand.
proposals.needs: S5 blueprint.twin (already in spec); F6 sets kind 'test' with cfg.twin (R18); S6 renders the diff and peer grids; F4 traps norm (R9); S2 classes for the assignment default. This matches the user's Daily Challenge decision (twins, so answers can't be passed around).

proposals.title: Paper question boards: every paper question with the crowd's answer spread and the trap that caught most people

They show no per-question statistics, and their distractor analysis is prose, not counts. proposals.title: Coverage-aware sections: each fresh test brings the question types you've met least, and the lobby says what it holds
proposals.what:
SERVER: blueprint.fill ranks each slot's candidate templates by (uses in this set, then learner exposure, then the current penalty). Exposure is the number of the learner's attempts plus practice_seen rows on that template. The blueprint's domain split, difficulty ladder and grid-in positions don't change, so the section stays representative and its estimate valid.
LOBBY: two fact rows are added:
- 'What it holds: Algebra 8 · Advanced Math 7 · Problem-Solving 4 · Geometry 3 · 6 grid-ins';
- '9 question types you've never met'. It is a count only; the names are withheld until hand-in.
REPORT (S6): 'New types this test: 9 · right on 5', with the list and a 'Practise' on each.
TESTS PAGE (under T4): 'Question types met under the clock: 142 of 386', with a quiet 'Which ones?'. It opens a list by skill in three groups: met in tests / practice only / never, with 'Practise the never-met' (pool untried).
START SHEET, Tools: a 'Favour types I haven't met' switch, on by default. Off gives today's scheduler.

proposals.title: Pencil-and-paper tests: print any test with an answer sheet, time it on screen, bubble in, get the full report
proposals.what:
START: step 4 adds 'Format: On screen / On paper'. For paper, the lobby shows the 'Print module 1' pill, 'Print answer sheet' and the proctor clock.
PRINT VIEW (/test/?s=ID&print=m1; Letter or A4, black on white):
- a cover with the directions and the reference sheet;
- questions in two columns, with SVG figures and grid-in boxes drawn;
- a bubble sheet: 22 rows of A-D, plus 5-box grid-in grids;
- the footer 'SAT Freshman · Full section #12 · Module 1 · print id'. No key anywhere.
PROCTOR SCREEN: a big DM Mono clock with Start and Pause (no pause in strict mode), the 5-minute notice, and 'Time' at 0.
ANSWER ENTRY (#enter):

proposals.title: How you take tests: a cross-sitting panel of test-taking habits, each with one fix
proposals.what:
SECTION: 'How you take tests' on /tests/, after T1, with its own section-nav item. Shown after 2 timed sittings. Each tile has a number, a trend against your previous 3 tests, and one action line:
1. End of module: 'Q17-22: 38% right · Q1-16: 71%', with an accuracy-by-position sparkline. Action: 'Hard-end practice: 10 hard at 95 s'.
2. Pace: median time by position against the pace line. 'You reach Q16 with 9:10 left on average.'
3. Time left at hand-in: '4:10 left and 1.2 blanks a module'. Action: 'Spend spare minutes on marked questions'.
4. Answer changes: '+5 net (7 wrong→right, 2 right→wrong): your second look pays'. When the net is negative: 'Change an answer only when you find an error.'
5. Mark for review: 'Marked 18 · went back to 15 · changed 6 · gained 4'.
6. Confidence, when the tags were used: 'Sure 91% right · Unsure 62% · Guess 30%'.
7. Calculator: 'Open on 40% of questions · 78% right with it, 64% without'.
8. Away: 'Left the window 3 times in 5 tests'.
9. Pressure, from proposal 1: 'Pressure losses: 3 a test, down from 5'.
FILTERS: Last 5 / 10 / All; Sections and papers / All timed. Each tile has a quiet 'Which sittings?' that sets the T6 filter.
SERVER: GET /api/tests adds habits{}, computed from qstate over timed, non-abandoned sittings. Older rows without qstate are counted out, and the tile says 'from 4 of 7 tests'.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep shows no test-taking behaviour at all: their report has no time per question, and they record no answer changes, no flag outcomes and no calculator use. Their contest 'Time analysis' was empty. Ours comes from per-question state the runner already stores.
proposals.needs: F4 qstate trail/first/changes/conf/ms/away (R7); a new qstate.calc_ms written by the runner (an F3 UI.calc hook); S6 per-sitting blocks as drill-down targets; proposal 1's result.pressure for tile 9; coordinate with S6 Results (its accuracy split is per difficulty only, not per habit).

proposals.title: Desmos coach: your calculator work kept per question, and the question already typed into Desmos in review
proposals.what:
RUNNER: records per question qstate.calc_ms (how long the calculator was open while on it) and calc_exprs (the expressions added while on it, up to 20 LaTeX strings, taken from getExpressions on move-away).
BANK: a template hook desmos(item) → [latex] for templates that graphing or a regression solves: linear and nonlinear equations, systems, quadratics and tangency, exponentials, regressions from tables. Start with about 80-120 templates. desmos_best: true when graphing is the faster route. An audit check confirms the expressions reproduce the key.
REVIEW (after hand-in, through deps.access):
- 'Your calculator on this question': a read-only Desmos showing your expressions, or 'Not used'.
- 'The Desmos way': opens Desmos preloaded with this seed's expressions (e.g. y=2x^2-6x and y=c/2 with a slider for c), plus one line of how: 'Slide c until the line touches the parabola once.'
REPORT (S6): 'Desmos was the quick route on 4 questions you did by hand (2:10 on average; the Desmos way takes about 0:40)'.
ELSEWHERE: the practice session's explanation gets the same 'Desmos way' for those templates.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep embeds Desmos but forgets its state and never shows when it is the fast route. Teaching it question by question would mean hand-writing every item. Our templates hold their own equations, so every seed can be typed into Desmos automatically.
proposals.needs: F3 UI.calc (per-sitting state is in spec) extended with per-question snapshots; a T-bank template hook desmos() plus its audit check; F4 deps.access (R19); the S6 review player button; S4 practice explanation.

proposals.title: Scratch work that's kept: a pen and typed scratch layer per question, shown beside the named mistake in review
proposals.what:
TOOL: 'Scratch' in the top-bar tools, key W (free in the §2.8 runner map). It toggles a transparent pen layer over the question column: pen, touch or mouse; 2 widths; graphite ink; an eraser; Clear. A 'Typed scratch' box under the options (monospace, 0/1000) serves keyboard users.
STORAGE: strokes are simplified (Ramer-Douglas-Peucker, 20 KB or less per question) and saved as qstate[qid].scratch through POST /state and the same save queue, so a reload keeps them. The text size and column width are recorded, so the overlay lines up again.
REVIEW (after hand-in): a 'Your work' toggle draws the strokes over the stem where they were made, next to the misconception the chosen option names. The student sees 'added the exponents' at the line where they did it.
PHONE: two fingers scroll while the pen is on, and a 'Done' button closes it.
STRICT: allowed in strict mode, since the real test gives scratch paper.
proposals.beats: Neither TopTierPrep nor Bluebook has a scratch area, so a student's working is lost and the review can't show where the reasoning went wrong. Ours keeps the work next to the misconception behind the chosen answer.
proposals.needs: An F3 runner tool slot and overlay (built alongside UI.annotate); an F4 qstate scratch field with a size cap (R7); the S6 review player overlay; F2 UI.keys W.

parity_gaps.feature: Number of papers on the shelf
parity_gaps.spec_says: Papers #1-#7 from mocks.json plus one new paper every Monday; 'Shows 6 papers, then Show all 8'.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: At launch that is 8 papers against their 29-31. The grid a TopTierPrep student opens looks a quarter the size, and the weekly drip is a scarcity we don't have.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Build 30 papers at launch: the 7 launch-set sections plus 23 from daily.paper seeds 'paper:launch-N', each excluding the others' items. Keep the weekly one. Pre-build the next 4 weeks lazily so no paper is ever built cold on a student's click.

parity_gaps.spec_says: Easier than most / Typical / Harder than most, measured from 20 or more first standard sittings; otherwise 'Not rated yet', and unrated papers sort last.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: On a new site every paper reads 'Not rated yet' for months. That is less than their editorial Easy/Medium/Hard label.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Predict the rating from day one: the paper's expected share of weight earned, from every learner's first-try accuracy per (template, tier) across all practice. It shows as 'Harder than most · predicted' and switches to 'measured from 34 sittings' at 20. Add 'Predicted for you: 540-620' on each card (estimate.projected run on that paper's items) and a 'Best for me' sort: most slots in your weakest skills and open traps.

parity_gaps.spec_says: Sat by / Average / You, plus 'New to you: 63 of 66' and 'your first sitting beats 62%'.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: The same information as their 'People took' and 'Your last score', better formatted.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Add 'Traps here you've fallen for: 3' (items whose distractors carry your traps) and 'You vs average: +40'. Add a 'Worth a retake' status: sat over 30 days ago, with 3 or more of its missed misconceptions fixed since. Its action is 'Retake as a twin', which counts as a fresh sitting for you but never toward the paper's stats.

parity_gaps.feature: Estimated score: empty state and trend
parity_gaps.spec_says: 'No estimate yet. A full section gives a band about 140 points wide...' until a scored sitting; the headline gives the trend since the last sitting.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It behaves exactly like theirs: nothing until a test, then a trend against the previous one.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Fill it from practice (proposal 2), with the empty state counting toward it ('38 of 60 answers'). Add a date forecast: 'At +12 a week over your last 5 sections: 610-690 by Oct 3', with a link to the plan's drift (R16 and S7 own the rule).

parity_gaps.spec_says: Rank among each learner's first standard sitting of the same kind (a paper: of that paper), shown from n 20 (30 on papers).
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: The same rule as their 'N% scored at or below you on their first attempt'.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Add cohort percentiles: among students with the same exam date ('among 214 sitting Oct 3') and the same target band. Two weeks before each official SAT date, release a paper for that date with its own cohort board (their 'September Predictions' papers, done honestly), coordinated with Compete's Season Final. Always print n.

parity_gaps.spec_says: A 4-step sheet: Test · Modules · Timing · Tools. A card's Start is one tap with your defaults.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Their 3-step wizard with a tools step added.
parity_gaps.upgrade: A presets row at the top of the sheet: 'Like test day' (strict, official, adaptive, no extras), 'Same as last time', 'Pacing practice', 'Accommodations 1.5x'. Each goes to the lobby in one tap, and the summary line names what the preset changed.

parity_gaps.spec_says: Official / time and a half / double / untimed count-up, and custom minutes.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Timed and Untimed are theirs; extended time is Bluebook's.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Add 'Tightening pace' training timing. It starts at 1.25x and tightens by 0.05 each sitting while accuracy holds within 5 points of the previous sitting, until it reaches official. Its line reads 'Pace training: 1.15x · 2 more sittings to official'. It is only practical because every sitting is fresh.

parity_gaps.spec_says: The lobby offers 'Enter fullscreen and begin' or 'Begin without fullscreen'. Save and exit pauses the clock, and pauses are shown on the report.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Fullscreen stays optional and has no consequence, as on theirs.

parity_gaps.spec_says: Q badge · Mark for review · confidence · Eliminate · Report.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: The same tool set as theirs (their Mark doubles as a save list).
parity_gaps.upgrade: Add 'Save for later' (key B, as in practice). The question goes to Review > Saved with the sitting's context, and its key shows after hand-in. Also use the stored strikes in the report: 'You struck the right answer on Q9', and 'The option you kept over the key was the trap: added the exponents'.

parity_gaps.spec_says: 7 styles in orange and graphite, a notes rail, and notes kept per (template, seed) (R6).
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Their 4 colours, 3 underlines and a note, restyled.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Let a note also attach to the question type. A note on a template is offered on its twins in review and practice ('Your note on this kind, Sep 12: square the radius first'). The notes rail can print as a per-skill 'My rules' sheet.

parity_gaps.spec_says: The existing UI.ref: a drawn SVG sheet in a dialog.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Their official image in a modal.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Templates tag the formula they use. The review highlights that line on the sheet ('It was on the reference sheet: V = πr²h'), and the runner records reference opens per question for the Test habits panel.

parity_gaps.spec_says: A keystroke filter, KaTeX preview, and the 'Entering your answer' rail or disclosure with the examples table.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Their SPR pane and preview; the filter is the only gain.

parity_gaps.spec_says: A legend with counts, the filters All / Unanswered / For review / Guesses, 40px cells, Esc and arrow keys.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Their popover with counts added.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Add a Time toggle, as on Check your work, and the personal pace marker on the cell you should be on. Add 'Next unanswered' and 'Next marked' buttons (with keys) so a student can sweep without opening the grid.

parity_gaps.spec_says: Three filter tiles, a Status/Time view, the no-penalty guessing tip and a pacing line.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Their page, with a time view and tips.
parity_gaps.upgrade: A coached triage (proposal 4): unanswered and marked questions ordered by expected points per minute, from your own accuracy and speed on each kind.

parity_gaps.spec_says: 'Module 1 is in' with tiles, the module 2 card and an optional 'You earned the harder module 2'.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: The same information as theirs and Bluebook's: no break, route hidden.
parity_gaps.upgrade: After the test, show the route margin on the report and the sittings row: 'routed up with 2 to spare', or '1 short: Q2 and Q5, both easy'. Link it to the Route-up trainer (proposal 5). Between modules, add a module 1 time profile: '3 questions took over 3:00'.

parity_gaps.spec_says: A 'Time's up' screen after the fact, and a 5-minute warning earlier.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Their behaviour, plus a message.
parity_gaps.upgrade: At 1:00 left with blanks, a banner: '3 unanswered. A guess can't cost you.' Its 'Go to next blank' cycles through the blanks and never fills anything in. The report counts 'blank at time' apart from blanks skipped earlier.

parity_gaps.spec_says: UI.report: 10 images, the category list, (template, seed) attached, and status shown in Me.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Their modal, with a status loop added.
parity_gaps.upgrade:
An instant independent re-check. On a key or answer category, the server regenerates the (template, seed) and runs the satbank.audit solver. After hand-in the student sees one of two verdicts:
- 'Checked: the independent solver agrees with C (65b²c²). Your B is what you get if you add the three coefficients.'
- 'The solver disagrees: your answer now counts, and this template is paused for everyone.' The answer is marked disputed (R8) and the template is quarantined until fixed.
Mid-test the verdict is held back (R17).

parity_gaps.spec_says: Gated threads, tagged by question, with Helpful, report-to-hide and a 20-a-day limit.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Their comments, with gating and question tags.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Question boards (proposal 7): the crowd's % right and a labelled answer spread per question, the paper's top traps, and 'your cheapest points', before any posts.

parity_gaps.spec_says: A link to the exact questions; both scores show once both have finished.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Their QBank share mechanics (link and copy), applied to tests.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Twin share by default (proposal 6): own numbers, so answers can't be copied, with a slot-by-slot peer comparison that names each person's misconception.

parity_gaps.feature: Assigning a test to a class
parity_gaps.spec_says: Classes live in Shell §7; the Tests share is called 'the equivalent of their teacher homework'.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Their hidden 'assign a full practice test' with a due date.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Every student gets a twin form, so there's no copying. The teacher sees a slot-by-slot class grid with each slot's misconception spread, and one tap assigns 'Fix the class's top 3 traps' as a follow-up drill.

parity_gaps.spec_says: 'Asks for your name and email before the result' (R38, pending open question 8).
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Worse than theirs: their diagnostic is hidden but not gated, and a gate conflicts with 'completely free, no paywalls'.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Show the result at once, like any sitting. After it, offer 'Keep this on your other devices: add an email'. The diagnostic stays the Up next default for new students.

parity_gaps.spec_says: Easy / Medium / Hard toggles (at least one), ladder or mixed order.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Their QBank difficulty filter.
parity_gaps.upgrade: An 'At my level' option: per skill, the tier where your first-try accuracy is between 50% and 75% (your frontier). Add 'Stretch' (one tier above). The summary line shows the tier chosen for each skill.
